title: Beyond Island Conservation: Spatial Ecology, Corridor Mechanics, and Policy Imperatives for Megafauna Connectivity
abstract: The long-term viability of terrestrial megafauna increasingly depends on landscape-scale connectivity rather than isolated protected reserves. As anthropogenic fragmentation intensifies, maintaining functional movement corridors is critical for preserving genetic diversity, mitigating environmental stochasticity, and preventing human-wildlife conflict. This paper synthesizes the ecological necessity of elephant corridors, the technological mechanics of spatial modeling and least-cost path identification, and the persistent operational bottlenecks posed by linear infrastructure and agricultural encroachment. Furthermore, we examine the evolution of legal frameworks and administrative mandates required to transition from defensive containment to integrated, landscape-level coexistence.
